brief: Garrett (GS FICC and equities) argues macro uncertainty is priced too cheaply: a hawkish global hiking cycle, oil above the $100 handle every day last week, unresolved Middle East escalation, US 10-year yields near 5% with GS raising year-end rate targets, AI-trade backlash the note calls the largest driver of US growth, and midterm elections under two months out, yet VIX closed at 14 with index and single-stock convexity near historic lows. His view: the market has begun to re-risk, and implied vol is cheap enough to express that via limited-loss structures, including lookback puts priced 60-100bps over the vanilla that guarantee selling the top. Desk trades include stock-replacing into the midterms, long QQQ versus short IWM on a breadth-won't-widen view, and a cybersecurity basket up 60% YTD. Positioning diverges: prime brokerage shows the largest net buying in five weeks with a defensive-to-offensive sector rotation, while the cash desk sees long-only selling in some of the same sectors; retail inflows hit $80bn last week despite bearish sentiment; FOMC-week options flow is bullish; FXI implied vol sits at multi-year lows ahead of a possible Trump-Xi summit; NVDA implied vol is at its lowest since before Covid.
